questionsToConsider: Which skills does each role truly depend on? Those belong in the confidence grid.
Do you need answers split by team or seniority, and does the form ask enough to do that?
Is there a set budget or time for training, and should the time question reflect it?
Will managers also assess their teams, so you can compare self-ratings with theirs?
guide.howToUseResponses: Count the "I need training" and "Some gaps" answers in the confidence grid for each team to find the biggest shared gaps. Read the stuck moments to understand what the gap looks like in practice, which helps a trainer pitch the content right. Match topics to the most popular formats and the time people can give, and use the people who said they could teach as in-house trainers or mentors before paying for outside courses.
customizeSteps: Replace the rows in the confidence grid with the skills your roles need, such as a named system, a sales process or a clinical procedure.
Edit the topic list to the training you could actually provide this year.
Share the link with each team through their manager, and export the answers to CSV to compare teams side by side.

faqs.q: What is a training needs assessment survey?
faqs.a: A survey that finds the gaps between the skills people have and the skills their work needs, so you plan training around real needs rather than guesses.

faqs.q: What questions should a training needs assessment include?
faqs.a: Questions about current tasks, confidence in key skills, recent situations where people got stuck, the topics they want and how they prefer to learn.

faqs.q: When should you run a training needs assessment?
faqs.a: Before planning a training budget or calendar, and after a big change such as new software, a new process or a new team structure.

faqs.q: Can I find in-house trainers with this survey?
faqs.a: Yes. Near the end it asks whether people could teach a topic, and only those who say yes are asked what they could share and how to reach them.
